paper.title: The Max $K$-Armed Bandit: PAC Lower Bounds and Efficient Algorithms

unmapped: Goal is to return a single sample whose value is within epsilon of the maximal support point mu* = max_k mu*_k with probability > 1-delta (max-value objective, not mean)
Assumption 1: the learner knows a function G_*(eps) and eps_0 lower-bounding every arm's tail function G_k(eps)=1-F_k(mu*_k-eps) for eps<=eps_0
Reward distributions arbitrary with finite maximal support point
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm is said to be (\epsilon,\delta)-correct if P(V>\maxmu-\epsilon)>1-\delta. ... Assumption 1: There exists a known function \FF(\epsilon) and a known constant \epsilon_0>0 such that, for every k\in K and 0\leq\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0, it holds that \OFF_k(\epsilon)\geq\FF(\epsilon)

settings.name_in_paper: Unified-arm model (arms sampled uniformly at random, not distinguishable)
unmapped: Learner cannot choose arms: each sample comes from a uniformly random arm (single mixture arm with CDF (1/K) sum_k F_k)
Goal: return a sample within epsilon of the maximal support point with probability > 1-delta
Learner knows tail lower bound G_*(eps) and eps_0 (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: In the unified-arm model, when the agent samples from this unified arm, one of the original arms is chosen uniformly at random, and a reward is sampled from this arm. The CDF of the unified arm is therefore F(\mu)=\frac{1}{|K|} \sum_{k\in \KK} F_k(\mu)

algorithms.name: Maximal Confidence Bound (Max-CB)
requires_knowledge_of: G_star (tail lower bound) and its inverse

symbols.G_star: known lower bound on the tail functions G_k(eps)=1-F_k(mu*_k - eps)
symbols.Theta_k: min{max(epsilon, mu_star - mu*_k), eps_0}, mu*_k maximal support point of arm k
symbols.sum_not_kstar: sum over all arms except one optimal arm k*
symbols.eps_0: range on which the tail lower bound holds

source.label: thm:lower:bound
source.quote: Let $k^*$ denote some optimal arm, such that $\mu^{*}_{k^*} = \maxmu$. Let Assumption \ref{assumption:1} holds with a concave function $\FF(\epsilon)$ and let $\epsilon\leq\epsilon_0$ and $\delta\leq\frac{3}{20}e^{-3}$. Then, for every $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct algorithm, E[T]\geq \sum_{k\in \KK\setminus \{k^*\}}\frac{1}{32\FF\left(\Theta_k\right)}\ln\left(\frac{3}{20\delta}\right)

results.notes: Sum excludes only one optimal arm (other optimal arms included). Algorithm class: (epsilon,delta)-correct algorithms.

symbols.G_star: known lower bound on the tail functions

tuning: N_0 = floor((L - ln delta)/eps_0) + 1 initial samples per arm

source.label: thm:alg1
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, for any $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ such that $\G\geq10$, Algorithm \ref{alg:example} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct with a sample complexity of E[T]\leq \sum_{k\in\KK}\frac{\G-\ln(\delta)}{\FF\left(\Theta_k\right)}+|\KK|

results.notes: Algorithm is also shown (epsilon,delta)-correct. Does not require concavity of G_star.

bound.expression: (1 - delta**alpha_r)*sum_arms((L_alg - log(delta))/G_star(Theta_bar_k)) + delta**alpha_r*(K*(L_alg - log(delta))/G_star(epsilon))**(1 - alpha_r) + K

symbols.G_star: tail lower bound given to the algorithm (too optimistic)
symbols.alpha_r: misspecification factor alpha<1: Assumption 1 holds for alpha*G_star
symbols.eps_prime: G_star^{-1}((K(L_alg - log delta))^{1-alpha_r} G_star(epsilon)^{alpha_r}), achieved accuracy

conditions: Assumption 1 does not hold for G_star but holds for alpha*G_star with alpha<1

source.label: prop:1
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption \ref{assumption:1} does not hold for $\FF(\epsilon)$, but holds for $\FF'(\epsilon)=\alpha\FF(\epsilon)$ for some $\alpha<1$. Then Algorithm \ref{alg:example} is $(\epsilon',\delta')$-correct with $\epsilon'=\FF^{-1}(...)$ and $\delta'=\delta^{\alpha}$, and sample complexity bound ...

results.notes: Robustness result; algorithm is (eps', delta^alpha)-correct rather than (epsilon,delta)-correct.

symbols.alpha_r: factor alpha>1 such that Assumption 1 also holds for alpha*G_star

conditions: Assumption 1 holds for G_star and also for alpha*G_star with alpha>1

source.label: prop:2
source.quote: When Assumption \ref{assumption:1} holds for $\FF(\epsilon)$, and also for $\FF'(\epsilon)=\alpha\FF(\epsilon)$ for some $\alpha>1$, and $\G\geq10$, Algorithm \ref{alg:example} is $(\epsilon,\delta')$-correct where $\delta'=\delta^{\alpha} e^{-(\alpha-1)L}$ ... with the sample complexity provided in Theorem \ref{thm:alg1}

results.notes: Bound on probability of returning a sample worse than mu*-epsilon (conservative tail estimate). Sample complexity is same as Theorem 2 (not separately recorded).

symbols.G_star: known lower bound on the tail functions

source.label: thm:lower:single
source.quote: For every $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct algorithm, under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, when $\FF(\epsilon)$ is concave and $\delta\leq\frac{3}{20}e^{-3}$, it holds that E[T]\geq \frac{|\KK|}{16\FF\left(\epsilon\right)}\ln\left(\frac{3}{20\delta}\right).

symbols.G_star: known lower bound on the tail functions

source.label: thm:alg:Single
source.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption:1}, Algorithm \ref{alg:example_S} is $(\epsilon,\delta)$-correct, with a sample complexity bound of E[T]\leq \frac{|\KK|\ln(\delta^{-1})}{\FF(\epsilon)}+2.
